title.en: An elevator going below the ground floor!

text.en:
In a mall lift, pressing +3 went three floors UP, 0 stopped at the ground, and pressing -2 went UNDERGROUND!
"Numbers live on BOTH sides of zero!" exclaimed Aarav.

Numbers don't stop at zero! Moving right or upward gives positive numbers (+1, +2, +3...), while moving left or downward below zero gives negative numbers (-1, -2, -3...). Together with 0, they form Integers.
Zero is neither positive nor negative—it is the neutral balance point.
Along a horizontal number line, numbers ALWAYS get larger as you move right and smaller as you move left: so -2 is greater than -5 (just as -2°C is warmer than -5°C!).
Imagine an elevator: +1, +2, +3 go above ground, 0 is ground floor, and -1, -2 go into underground parking!
Whole numbers, zero and negative counting numbers (...-3, -2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +3...) together are called Integers.
Where do negative numbers appear in real life? Winter temperatures like -8°C in Ladakh, basement floors, sea depths and bank debits!
Zero itself is special: 0 is neither positive nor negative—it sits right in the middle!
Line integers evenly along a ruler: +1, +2, +3 march to the right of 0; -1, -2, -3 mirror cleanly to the left of 0!
Remember the golden rule of the number line: numbers ALWAYS grow LARGER going RIGHT and SMALLER going LEFT!

board.text: Further right = larger; Further left = smaller

text.en: Check carefully: between -2 and -7, which is larger? -2 sits closer to 0 (to the right of -7), so -2 > -7!
Opposite pairs like +5 and -5 sit equal distance from 0 on opposite sides—and adding opposites (+5) + (-5) lands right back on 0 (Bela's zero-pair!).
And what about moving along the line? Starting at -3 and moving 5 steps RIGHT (+5) passes 0 and lands on +2!
So whenever negative numbers feel tricky, picture a thermometer or number line: moving up/right adds, moving down/left subtracts!

problem.en: Order these temperatures from coldest (smallest) to warmest (largest): 4°C, -9°C, 0°C, -2°C.

why.en: -9°C is 9 steps below zero, and -2°C is 2 steps below zero -> -9°C is colder (-9 < -2).
0°C sits above all negative temperatures, and +4°C sits warmer than 0°C.

prompt.en: Why is -3 greater than -10 even though 10 looks like a bigger digit than 3?

requiredIdeas.en: -10°C is much colder and farther left of zero than -3°C.
On a number line, -3 sits to the right of -10, so -3 > -10.

points.en: Integers = negative integers, 0, and positive integers.
Moving right increases value; moving left decreases value.
For negatives, closer to 0 means greater (-2 > -7).
